articles.title: Governo amplia Contrata+Brasil e cria sistema de compras online | G1
articles.standfirst: Novo sistema permitirá uso de plataformas digitais nas compras governamentais; Contrata+Brasil passa a incluir estatais e amplia o número de atividades disponíveis para microempreendedores individuais.
articles.summary: Novo sistema permitirá compras por plataformas digitais; Contrata+Brasil passa a incluir estatais e amplia atividades disponíveis para MEIs.
articles.body:
O evento também marcou o lançamento do programa Contrata+Brasil em Campinas, iniciativa do Governo Federal que facilita a conexão entre órgãos públicos e fornecedores locais, ampliando oportunidades para MEIs, pequenos negócios, cooperativas e agricultores familiares — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação/PPM Films.

O governo federal anunciou nesta segunda-feira (24) a regulamentação do Sistema de Compras Expressas (Sicx) e mudanças no Contrata+Brasil , plataforma que conecta microempreendedores individuais (MEIs) a órgãos públicos interessados em contratar pequenos serviços.

🗒️ Tem alguma sugestão de reportagem? Mande para o g1

As medidas têm como objetivo modernizar as compras públicas, ampliar a participação de fornecedores e facilitar o acesso de pequenos empreendedores a contratos com o governo.

Criado para facilitar a participação de MEIs em pequenas contratações feitas pelo poder público, o Contrata+Brasil ampliou de 137 para 272 o número de atividades econômicas de prestação de serviços disponíveis na plataforma . ( veja a lista completa abaixo )

➡️ LISTA DE SERVIÇOS DE MANUTENÇÃO E PEQUENOS REPAROS

Inicialmente, eram apenas 47 serviços. A expansão também inclui a adesão formal de empresas públicas, estatais e autarquias , como Banco do Brasil, Caixa Econômica Federal, Banco do Nordeste, Correios, Petrobras e INSS.

Na prática, essas instituições poderão utilizar a plataforma para encontrar MEIs que prestem serviços como reparos, pintura, carpintaria e manutenção.

Segundo a ministra da Gestão e da Inovação em Serviços Públicos, Esther Dweck, um dos principais objetivos da iniciativa é reduzir o tempo e a burocracia das contratações e aumentar a renda dos pequenos empreendedores.

“Uma contratação que demorava quase seis meses entre contratar o serviço, ser prestado e pagar foi feita em cinco dias em alguns casos. Então é uma velocidade gigantesca”, afirmou.

“Muitos MEIs têm um faturamento de R$ 2 mil, R$ 3 mil por mês. E os contratos públicos são, em geral, em torno de R$ 8 mil. Então, às vezes, com um contrato público, a pessoa ganha o dinheiro que demorava o mês inteiro para ganhar”, completou.

O acesso é gratuito tanto para os empreendedores quanto para os órgãos públicos. Não há cobrança de taxas ou comissões.

Segundo o governo, existem atualmente 13,7 milhões de MEIs ativos no Brasil . Dados do Sebrae citados pelo Ministério da Gestão mostram que 51,6% dos MEIs têm interesse em vender para o governo, mas apenas 13,6% já fizeram algum negócio com a administração pública .

A proposta é ampliar essa participação e facilitar o acesso dos pequenos empreendedores às oportunidades de contratação.

A entrada das novas instituições representa, segundo o governo, mais de 14,7 mil unidades públicas que poderão contratar serviços por meio da plataforma .

A iniciativa também será incentivada em cerca de 109 mil escolas públicas que recebem recursos do Programa Dinheiro Direto na Escola (PDDE).

Somadas as unidades das estatais e autarquias às escolas, o governo estima um universo potencial de aproximadamente 123 mil pontos de contratação para pequenos serviços em todo o país.

Isso, no entanto, não significa que existam 123 mil vagas ou contratos disponíveis para os MEIs . O número representa a quantidade potencial de unidades que poderão utilizar a plataforma para fazer contratações.

Uma das frentes de expansão do Contrata+Brasil será o Programa Dinheiro Direto na Escola (PDDE), que está em vigor desde o início do ano.

Segundo o governo, cerca de 109 mil escolas públicas recebem recursos do programa , que movimenta aproximadamente R$ 933 milhões em despesas de custeio.

Entre os gastos estão pequenos reparos, pintura, carpintaria e serviços de manutenção — atividades que podem ser realizadas por MEIs. A ideia é facilitar a contratação de prestadores de serviços da própria região.

O presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva afirmou, durante o evento de lançamento das medidas, que a iniciativa pode ajudar a manter a circulação de dinheiro dentro das cidades. “Se a diretora da escola souber que pode contratar um prestador de serviço na sua própria cidade, o dinheiro vai ficar ali".

Plataforma quer aumentar participação de MEIs

O Contrata+Brasil funciona como uma plataforma que conecta pequenos prestadores de serviços a órgãos públicos. O MEI pode procurar oportunidades de acordo com sua atividade e região e enviar uma proposta diretamente pelo sistema.

De acordo com o governo, os MEIs representam atualmente 4,7% do valor total contratado pelo Compras.gov.br, apesar de somarem 13,7 milhões de empreendedores ativos no país.

A pesquisa do Sebrae citada pelo Executivo mostra que 51,6% dos MEIs têm interesse em vender para o governo, mas apenas 13,6% já fizeram alguma transação com a administração pública.

A proposta é reduzir as dificuldades de acesso às compras públicas, especialmente para serviços de menor porte. Segundo Esther Dweck, o sistema permite contratações diretas de MEIs para serviços de até R$ 13 mil, dentro das regras aplicáveis.

“O governo federal representa cerca de 5,6% a 6% do PIB em compras; é o maior comprador do país. Se ele passa a exigir a compra dos pequenos em todo local, ele vai desenvolver a economia”, afirmou a ministra.

Entre as instituições que aderiram ao programa estão:

Caixa Econômica Federal: 3.258 unidades;

Também já participam ministérios da administração direta, como Defesa, Saúde, Educação e Agricultura.

Segundo o governo, a adesão amplia em cerca de 60 vezes o número de potenciais contratantes na plataforma . A iniciativa também prevê uma busca ativa por empreendedores .

Em vez de depender apenas da procura dos MEIs pelas oportunidades, a proposta é que o poder público também identifique prestadores de serviços que possam atender às demandas existentes.

Além das mudanças no Contrata+Brasil, o governo regulamentou o Sistema de Compras Expressas (Sicx), voltado para a contratação de bens e serviços padronizados pela administração pública.

O decreto assinado pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva estabelece regras para o uso de plataformas de comércio eletrônico nas compras governamentais.

A proposta permite que fornecedores utilizem plataformas digitais que já fazem parte de suas atividades comerciais. Com isso, o governo pretende aproveitar tecnologias já disponíveis no mercado e reduzir os custos de adaptação.

O modelo também prevê um cadastro digital permanente, integrado ao Registro Cadastral Unificado (RCU). A medida pretende evitar que o fornecedor precise apresentar os mesmos documentos a cada nova oportunidade de contratação.

Segundo o governo, o lançamento do RCU está previsto para o último trimestre de 2026. O Sicx faz parte da Estratégia Nacional de Contratações Públicas para o Desenvolvimento Sustentável (ENCP), que busca usar as compras do governo para estimular o desenvolvimento econômico e sustentável.

O microempreendedor pode acessar a plataforma e procurar oportunidades de contratação de acordo com sua atividade e região.

O acesso ao Contrata+Brasil é gratuito. Não há cobrança de taxa ou comissão para o empreendedor nem para o órgão público. Para participar, é necessário:

acessar a plataforma com uma conta gov.br;

procurar oportunidades compatíveis com seu perfil;

enviar uma proposta com o valor e o prazo para execução.

Caso seja escolhido, o MEI é contratado diretamente pelo órgão público por meio da plataforma. Atualmente, o Contrata+Brasil reúne 272 atividades econômicas (CNAEs) de prestação de serviços. A plataforma está disponível no site oficial do Contrata+Brasil .

Tela do site 'Contrata+Brasil', lançado pelo governo federal — Foto: PR/Reprodução

articles.title: Veja como é o acionamento do paraquedas do monomotor que caiu na Região Metropolitana de BH; piloto sobreviveu | G1
articles.standfirst: O Centro de Investigação e Prevenção de Acidentes Aeronáuticos vai apurar o que levou um avião a cair na zona rural de Mateus Leme.
articles.summary: O Centro de Investigação e Prevenção de Acidentes Aeronáuticos vai apurar o que levou um avião a cair na zona rural de Mateus Leme.
articles.body:
No Brasil, o Cenipa vai investigar a queda de um avião na Região Metropolitana de Belo Horizonte . O piloto sobreviveu depois de acionar o paraquedas do monomotor.

“A gente não sabia para onde correr porque pensou que ele ia cair em cima da gente”, conta a lavradora Fabrícia Macieira.

“Todo mundo correndo. Como já sou idosa, eu caí espichadinha no chão, sabe?”, diz a lavradora Maura Pereira da Silva.

O monomotor, que tinha um paraquedas acoplado, foi perdendo altitude de forma lenta, em meio a muita fumaça, até atingir o chão. O piloto saiu do avião pouco antes do fogo destruir toda a estrutura.

“Foi bom ver ele saindo lá de dentro e que não tinha machucado”, diz o lavrador Mateus Macieira.

Piloto de monomotor sobrevive após acionar paraquedas do avião — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Este modelo de monomotor tem uma alavanca que fica no teto da cabine. Em caso de emergência, ela pode ser acionada e abre um paraquedas que fica na parte de cima do avião, o que permite uma descida mais controlada. O avião tinha certificado de verificação válido e aparece com situação normal no Registro Aeronáutico Brasileiro.

Quando as equipes de resgate chegaram no local do acidente, o piloto estava consciente e entrou andando no helicóptero dos bombeiros. Gustavo Couto de Salles, de 29 anos, estava sozinho no avião. Ele teve ferimentos leves, mas inalou muita fumaça. Foi levado para um hospital em Belo Horizonte e teve alta durante a tarde desta terça-feira (25). O Gustavo saiu sorridente e aliviado.

“Toda hora pedindo a Deus para lembrar de todas as coisas que têm que ser feitas. Eu acredito que o paraquedas me ajudou muito, porque com a fumaça dentro da cabine, fica difícil você fazer todos os controles da aeronave, sabe?", diz o piloto Gustavo Couto de Salles.

Gustavo foi para casa comemorar duplamente. O filhinho dele completa dois meses nesta quarta-feira (26).

“Está comemorando hoje e amanhã. Aniversário dele hoje e do nosso filho amanhã. Para mim é incrível, melhor presente que eu poderia ter”, diz a advogada Brenda Monteiro Couto, mulher de Gustavo.

articles.title: Quaest: veja como está a disputa pelo Senado no DF | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa divulgada nesta terça (25) foi encomendada pela Globo. Na pesquisa espontânea, em que os nomes dos pré-candidatos não são mostrados aos eleitores, 73% estão indecisos.
articles.summary: Pesquisa Quaest para o Senado no DF mostra Michelle Bolsonaro com 25% e Leila do Vôlei com 17%, enquanto 73% dos eleitores seguem indecisos na consulta espontânea.
articles.body:
Pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta terça-feira (25) mostra como está a disputa pelo Senado no Distrito Federal. O levantamento foi encomendado pela Globo.

Em 2026, serão eleitos dois senadores em cada estado e no Distrito Federal, para renovar 54 das 81 cadeiras.

➡️Por isso, cada eleitor precisa votar em dois candidatos diferentes.

➡️Não é possível escolher o mesmo nome duas vezes.

Na pesquisa espontânea da Quaest — em que os nomes não são mostrados aos eleitores entrevistados —, 73% estão indecisos, porque não souberam citar um candidato .

Já na pesquisa estimulada, a lista de candidatos é mostrada, e cada entrevistado precisa responder duas vezes em quem pretende votar: para a primeira vaga e, depois, para a segunda vaga.

Michelle Bolsonaro (PL); Leila do Vôlei (PDT); Erika Kokay (PT) e Bia Kicis (PL) são candidatas ao Senado pelo DF. — Foto: Alan Santos/PR; Carlos Moura/Agência Senado; Kayo Magalhães/Câmara dos Deputados e Bruno Spada/Câmara dos Deputados

Os resultados da pesquisa para o Senado consideram as menções para a primeira e a segunda vagas em um total que soma 100% das intenções de voto e mantém a proporção entre candidatos, brancos/nulos e indecisos.

A Quaest ouviu 1.104 pessoas de 16 anos ou mais entre os dias 21 e 24 de agosto. A margem de erro é de 3 pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos, e o nível de confiança é de 95%. O número de registro no TSE é DF-06256/2026 .

Agora, veja os resultados que consideram apenas as respostas para a primeira vaga e, depois, para a segunda.

Para 55% dos eleitores ouvidos no levantamento, a escolha do candidato é definitiva. Outros 45% dizem que ainda podem mudar o voto até as eleições, em 4 de outubro.

Abaixo, veja os dados completos da pesquisa espontânea.

A Quaest perguntou também aos eleitores sobre cada um dos candidatos: se eles conhecem e votariam, se não conhecem ou se conhecem e não votariam. Os candidatos mais rejeitados (maiores índices de "conhece e não votaria") são Michelle Bolsonaro e Erika Kokay.

articles.title: VÍDEO: cobra 'sobe' escada submersa em rio de águas cristalinas em MT | G1
articles.standfirst: Guia de turismo Everton Strey mantém acervo de registros de sucuri-verde feitos durante passeios em Nobres (MT); ao g1, especialista dá dicas de como agir ao se deparar com a espécie.
articles.summary: Vídeo de encontro com sucuri-verde em Nobres viraliza e destaca a beleza do ecoturismo em Mato Grosso, com orientações de especialistas sobre a segurança durante a flutuação.
articles.body:
De escadas submersas ao fundo de rios de águas cristalinas, o guia de turismo Everton Strey acumulou registros de encontros com sucuris durante as flutuações, em Nobres , a 123 km de Cuiabá. Um dos vídeos mostra uma serpente se movimentando por degraus de escada dentro da água, a poucos metros do guia (assista acima).

Apesar da proximidade , o animal não avança em direção de Everton. Nas imagens, é possível ver a sucuri-verde submersa enquanto é acompanhada pelo guia. Ao g1, ele afirmou que o registro do animal na escada foi feito em 2023, mas foi recompartilhado recentemente e voltou a ganhar repercussão.

“Apesar de eu ter um pouco de costume de encontrar, confesso que dá um pouco de receio estar com o animal, mas é uma experiência fascinante”, afirmou.

✅ Clique aqui para seguir o canal do g1 MT no WhatsApp

O vídeo que voltou a circular nas redes sociais é apenas um dos inúmeros registros feitos por Everton durante os passeios no Reino Encantado, em Nobres. Everton disse que, como funcionário do local, acompanha a fauna encontrada nos rios e registra os animais durante as atividades.

Sucuri-verde é registrada descendo uma escada submersa durante flutuação em rio de águas cristalinas em Nobres (MT). — Foto: Everton Strey

Segundo Suely Oliveira, recepcionista do local onde os vídeos foram registrados, a quantidade de encontros de Everton com sucuris varia ao longo dos anos.

“O Everton é quem faz a maioria dos registros por aqui. Tem anos em que temos mais registros e outros em que temos menos. Neste ano, tivemos mais encontros”, afirmou.

De acordo com Suely, os registros são feitos de forma segura para preservar o comportamento natural dos animais, sem interferência ou aproximação que possa causar estresse ou alterar a rotina da espécie.

“Sempre procuramos registrar o animal à distância, respeitando o espaço e o comportamento dele”, completou.

Lobo-guará ou lobisomem? Hóspede sai do quarto para buscar Wi-Fi e se depara com fêmea no Pantanal de MT

VÍDEO: pescador se distrai e leva mordida de dourado em MT

🐍 Sucuri-verde é maior serpente do Brasil em massa corporal

Ao g1 , a bióloga Angélica Gomes da Silva explicou detalhes sobre o comportamento da sucuri-verde (Eunectes murinus) . Segundo ela é a maior serpente do Brasil em massa corporal, podendo atingir 8 metros de comprimento e pesar até 250 kg , e alimenta-se principalmente de peixes e anfíbios, além de aves, répteis e mamíferos, como outras serpentes e capivaras.

Apesar de não ser peçonhenta, ela explicou que se trata de um animal que utiliza da constrição para imobilizar e capturar presas. Após a alimentação, costuma entrar em estado de descanso, e ressaltou a importância de que os humanos respeitem esse período.

"Nada impede que aconteça um ataque, se o animal se sentir acuado. Por isso, é crucial evitar se aproximar desses indivíduos, e caso ela se afaste não ir atrás, porque o fato dela estar se afastando já é um indício de que está incomodada com a presença humana", destacou.

Ela também orientou sobre como agir ao encontrar uma sucuri-verde , destacando que não há, até o momento, a confirmação de que sucuris tenham humanos como preferência de presa.

“A sucuri não tem o ser humano como presa habitual, mas pode atacar por ter um comportamento defensivo [....] por isso, a melhor forma de se manter seguro é manter sempre distância e evitar movimentos bruscos que assustem o animal”, disse.

A região de Nobres integra a lista dos 15 principais destinos para visitar no Brasil em 2026, divulgado pela plataforma PlanetaExo , que tem como foco destinos com forte potencial para o ecoturismo, levando em conta critérios como preservação ambiental, diversidade de biomas e a oferta de experiências voltadas ao turismo sustentável.

Os encontros registrados por Everton acontecem em uma região conhecida pelos rios de águas cristalinas, nascentes e áreas de mata chamada Bom Jardim, um distrito a aproximadamente 65 km de distância da prefeitura municipal da cidade.

Se os vídeos gravados com as sucuris despertaram a curiosidade sobre as águas cristalinas de Mato Grosso, a região de Nobres reserva uma série de opções para quem deseja se conectar com a natureza. Para além das flutuações, o g1 preparou uma lista que reúne atrativos turísticos da região pelo tipo de passeio.

Cachoeira Serra Azul: Ponto turístico com queda d'água, trilha e atividades de aventura com a presença de uma tirolesa.

Duto do Quebó: Passeio de boia-cross realizado em um trecho do rio que passa por uma formação natural.

Lagoa das Araras: Local destinado à observação de aves, especialmente araras-canindé, com visitação voltada à contemplação da fauna.

Mirante do Cerrado: Ponto de observação da paisagem e do pôr do sol na região.

Balneário Estivado: Área de banho e lazer em meio à natureza, com presença de peixes e outros animais.

Reino Encantado: Atrativo de flutuação em águas cristalinas e local onde foram feitos os registros das sucuris-verdes.

Aquário Encantado: Nascente de águas cristalinas utilizada para flutuação, com percurso que segue pelo Rio Salobra.

Rio Triste: Trecho utilizado para flutuação e observação da vida aquática.

Vale das Águas: Área de flutuação no Rio Salobra, com águas cristalinas e contato com a fauna e a vegetação da região .

articles.standfirst: Polícia afirma que homens armados fugiram para uma área de mata na Favela do Lixo. Operação ocorreu nesta terça-feira (25).
articles.summary: Polícia afirma que homens armados fugiram para uma área de mata na Favela do Lixo. Operação ocorreu nesta terça-feira (25).
articles.body:
Grande quantidade de maconha foi apreendida em Cabo Frio após ação da PM — Foto: PM

A Polícia Militar apreendeu 667 porções de maconha e apreendeu um adolescente de 16 anos na tarde desta terça-feira (25), na Favela do Lixo, em Cabo Frio , na Região dos Lagos do Rio.

Segundo a PM, a ocorrência começou após denúncia sobre a chegada de uma grande quantidade de drogas à comunidade.

As equipes foram até uma área conhecida como Chiqueiro e encontraram cerca de seis suspeitos. Ainda conforme o relato policial, alguns deles estavam armados e efetuaram disparos contra os agentes ao perceberem a aproximação das equipes.

📱 Siga o canal do g1 Região dos Lagos no WhatsApp.

Os homens fugiram em direção a uma área de mata. Durante o cerco realizado pelos policiais, o adolescente foi localizado e apreendido. Os demais envolvidos não haviam sido encontrados até o encerramento da ocorrência.

No local, os agentes encontraram a droga em dois sacos pretos. O material foi encaminhado à delegacia de Cabo Frio.

O caso foi registrado por ato infracional análogo aos crimes de tráfico e associação para o tráfico.

articles.title: Diretor da CIA visita Moscou em viagem não confirmada, diz imprensa | G1
articles.standfirst: Pela manhã, uma aeronave militar americana decolou da Letônia com destino ao Aeroporto Vnukovo de Moscou, segundo dados do site de informações de voos Flightradar24.
articles.summary: Dados de voo e relatos da imprensa indicam que o diretor da CIA esteve em Moscou nesta terça-feira (25).
articles.body:
O diretor da agência de inteligência dos Estados Unidos (CIA), John Ratcliffe, visitou Moscou, na Rússia, nesta terça-feira (25), segundo a imprensa norte-americana.

✅ Siga o canal de notícias internacionais do g1 no WhatsApp

A informação foi divulgada pela rede de TV CBS e pelo site de notícias Axios. Ambos citaram fontes do governo norte-americano, que não disseram o motivos da viagem.

Estados Unidos e Rússia não confirmam oficialmente a visita, porém dados do site de informações de voos Flightradar24 mostram que, pela manhã, uma aeronave militar americana decolou da Letônia com destino ao Aeroporto Vnukovo de Moscou. Mais tarde, a plataforma mostrou que o mesmo avião deixou a capital russa.

O diretor da CIA John Ratcliffe, em imagem de arquivo. — Foto: Saul Loeb/AFP

A aeronave rastreada é um grande Boeing Globemaster, com a matrícula americana 07-7181. O voo de ida teria ocorrido por volta das 4h do horário de Brasília. A aeronave havia chegado a Riga em 23 de agosto vinda da base aérea americana de Camp Springs, perto de Washington.

Questionado sobre o voo em coletiva com jornalistas pela manhã, o porta-voz do Kremlin disse não ter informações.

Vídeo gravado por testemunhas oculares mostra avião de transporte militar dos EUA em aproximação para pouso em Moscou. — Foto: REUTERS

Segundo o jornal "Financial Times", os Estados Unidos pediram à Ucrânia que não atacasse Moscou, São Petersburgo nem outras zonas do norte da Rússia entre esta segunda-feira (24) e esta quarta-feira (26), a fim de permitir a viagem de uma autoridade americana. O pedido foi aceito.

Diversos temas podem justificar esse deslocamento pouco habitual do principal responsável pela espionagem externa dos Estados Unidos: a guerra na Ucrânia, o conflito com o Irã em um momento em que Washington se esforça para reunir potências estrangeiras em torno de sua estratégia de pressão econômica sobre Teerã, ou até mesmo trocas de prisioneiros.

Em outras ocasiões, o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, mandou seu genro Jared Kushner e o enviado especial Steve Witkoff a Moscou para diálogos com o presidente russo.

articles.title: UK drone factories may face attacks from 'unknown sources', says former Russian minister
articles.summary: The comments on BBC Newsnight come after the UK announced it has agreed to hand over blueprints for British-made missile components to Ukraine.
articles.body:
A Russian former deputy foreign minister has said there might be a "semi-military" response against UK drone factories by "unknown sources" over the sharing of blueprints for British-made cruise missile components .

Andrei Fedorov's comments on BBC Newsnight come as UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced plans to travel to the US next month with European leaders to lobby President Donald Trump on Ukraine's defence needs.

Burnham's trip, should it go ahead, would be his first to the US since becoming prime minister.

"Leaving today, I'm quite clear what I need to do in the next few weeks," he said following his visit to Ukraine on Monday, during which he promised to continue pressuring Russia.

The UK has agreed to hand over blueprints for British-made components for the Scalp missile , a French version of the UK's Storm Shadow cruise missile. The blueprints will allow Ukraine to produce the long-range weapon domestically.

Fedorov, a pro-Kremlin commentator who frequently appears on Russian television, said Putin was facing "serious" pressure "to undertake certain measures against UK". Asked on BBC Newsnight where the pressure was coming from, Fedorov responded "public opinion polls, it's coming from journalists, from mass media".

Asked what a "semi-military" response might look like, Fedorov said: "It could take the form of something might happen with enterprises, with factories which are producing drones for Ukraine.

"They could be attacked not by Russia, but by from unknown sources."

The comments are in line with those made by Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov on Monday, when he criticised the UK's decision to share the missile blueprints. Peskov said it prevented "even the slightest progress" towards achieving peace.

He told reporters on Monday that the Russian military was already gathering data to locate any missile production sites to destroy them.

"Britain is involved in this war on the side of the Kyiv regime. Britain methodically and regularly adds fuel to the fire," he added.

In response, Burnham said: "Who started the fire? That's the question, isn't it?"

Burnham's visit to Ukraine was his first official international trip. He met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Kyiv and chaired his first meeting of the "coalition of the willing", set up by the UK and France under his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer.

Burnham has been reaffirming the UK's support for Ukraine in the wake of escalating Russian strikes in recent weeks - including one last week on a shopping centre that killed at least 16 people.

Ukraine has been relying on American supplies of the Patriot interceptor missiles, which are used to combat Russia's ballistic missiles , but stockpiles are running low due to the war in Iran, leaving Ukraine vulnerable to Russian attacks.

Zelensky has said he is hoping to secure 300 patriot missiles ahead of winter, when Russia is likely to increase its attacks on energy infrastructure, as it has done in past years.

In the interview with Bloomberg, Burnham said he felt "really confident" that the issue was "fixable". But he pointed out that it wasn't only the US who could supply Ukraine with Patriots.

"There are other players who could help in the mix who we have influence with," he said. "It's probably going to be a solution that involves a lot of layers and a lot of negotiation."

In July this year, three weeks after offering Ukraine the right to produce Patriots itself, Trump backtracked, saying : "We have not agreed to that. We're talking about it. But it's a hard thing to give away, that kind of technology."

"These weapons are incredible. We have to be very careful about letting somebody build them," Trump told a cabinet meeting.

In a joint statement after the meeting in Ukraine, Burnham and co-chairs French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the group would aim to strength Kyiv's air defences "as a matter or urgent priority".

They also condemned Moscow's "systemic and escalating strikes against Ukraine's cities, critical infrastructure and civilians" and pledged to "constrain Russia's war chest through sanctions and actions against the shadow fleet".

In a statement ahead of the visit, Burnham said: "On Ukraine's 35th anniversary of independence, the Ukrainian people should be in no doubt: the UK is behind you today and for as long as it takes.

"I am proud of the contribution our country has made to Ukraine and I want the Ukrainian people to hear it directly from me that our support will not waver. After all, Ukraine's security is our security."

He said the friendship Ukraine shared with the UK would "long outlast Russia's illegal war", adding: "Russia should be in no doubt of our resolve. We will not back down until there is a just and lasting peace."

articles.title: Pakistan army officer pulls gun, fires in air amid student protest at Peshawar university- video
articles.summary: Pakistan News: A Pakistan army officer opened fire into the air during a student protest at Sarhad University in Peshawar, triggering chaos and a scuffle on the camp.
articles.body: A Pakistan army officer opened fire into the air during a student protest at Sarhad University in Peshawar, triggering chaos and a scuffle on the campus, according to local media reports and videos circulating online.The incident comes amid growing unrest in Pakistan, with protests and demonstrations also being reported from Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and Balochistan, adding to the challenges facing the country's military and political establishment.According to reports, the officer, said to be a colonel, was the husband of a faculty member at Sarhad University. He reportedly got into a heated confrontation with protesting students, which soon escalated into a physical scuffle.Videos shared by several social media accounts purportedly show the officer striking students with a stick amid the confrontation. As tensions escalated, he allegedly pulled out a pistol and initially pointed it towards the protesters before raising the weapon in the air.The officer was then seen firing shots into the air, sparking panic and further uproar on the university campus.Reports said the officer has been taken into custody, while the Pakistan army has ordered an inquiry into the incident.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: LSU women's basketball loses Kate Koval, a Ukrainian, days after Tigers sign Russian center
articles.summary: Kate Koval is from Kyiv, and her father is part of the Ukrainian military and has fought in the war against Russia.
articles.body:
Kim Mulkey lost a key piece to her frontcourt suddenly on Monday.

LSU women's basketball announced that center Kate Koval opted to leave the program due to personal reasons.

"Kate came to see me on Sunday and told me that after much consideration, she will be leaving the program for personal reasons," Mulkey said in a statement. "We will respect her privacy on her decision, but we had a long talk about it, and it was a hard decision for her. I know it is hard because she loves LSU. Kate is a great person. She has to do what she feels is right for her, and we fully support her in that. We wish her all the best."

A Statement From Head Coach Kim Mulkey: pic.twitter.com/vIkici06aH — LSU Women's Basketball (@LSUwbkb) August 24, 2026

A Statement From Head Coach Kim Mulkey: pic.twitter.com/vIkici06aH

Koval transferred to LSU last season after starting her career at Notre Dame. She started 17 games and averaged 8.3 points and 6.3 rebounds while shooting 56% from the field. She helped LSU reach the Sweet 16. It's unclear where Koval will end up playing next, though she can not join a new program for the 2026-27 campaign.

While specifics of her departure aren't known, there is speculation that it has to do with LSU's signing of 17-year-old Anna Minaeva.

Enes Kanter Freedom not welcome back at Sky home games after ejection, confrontation: 'He made himself into a threat'

Dream star Angel Reese grabs historic 26 rebounds in win over Sparks, passes A'ja Wilson for single-season record

PWHL's Walter Cup trophy has been found, league says, after briefly going missing

The Tigers landed Minaeva, also a center, earlier this month out of Russia. Koval is from Kyiv, Ukraine, so the two would have been what was believed to be the first Russian-Ukrainian teammates to share a locker room in women's college basketball since Russia first invaded Ukraine in 2022. Minaeva previously played professionally with MBA Moscow.

Koval's father, Oleksander, is also part of the Ukrainian military and has fought in the conflict.

Mulkey told The Advocate that she talked to Koval before recruiting Minaeva.

"I want you to understand I'm not here to ask you to change how you feel about Russia," Mulkey said, recalling her conversation with Koval. "I'm just here out of respect for your family and out of respect for you to let you know. Because I know how personal it is for you. "Know that what I have to do in this business, I cannot make a decision to not recruit somebody that can help our program because of a conflict between two countries."

"I want you to understand I'm not here to ask you to change how you feel about Russia," Mulkey said, recalling her conversation with Koval. "I'm just here out of respect for your family and out of respect for you to let you know. Because I know how personal it is for you.

"Know that what I have to do in this business, I cannot make a decision to not recruit somebody that can help our program because of a conflict between two countries."

Mukley is set to enter her sixth season leading the Tigers this fall. They will open the season against Southeast Louisiana on Nov. 2.

"Know that what I have to do in this business, I cannot make a decision to not recruit somebody that can help our program because of a conflict between two countries."
Mukley is set to enter her sixth season leading the Tigers this fall. They will open the season against Southeast Louisiana on Nov. 2.

articles.title: The Gurkha families in Reading fighting for their pensions
articles.summary: Gurkhas who retired before 1997 receive far less than their British Army counterparts.
articles.body:
Now aged 87, Indumati Thapa's life revolves around a group of similarly widowed women. Her husband, a former Gurkha who fought alongside the British in south east Asia, died in 2020.

He left her a pension, but Gurkhas who retired before 1997 receive far less than their British Army counterparts.

Theirs are based on Nepalese living costs, not those of towns like Reading, where thousands of Gurkhas retired to.

Indumati says her pension is so small she has to rely on the generosity of friends, and roughly Â£100 a week in benefits, to cover her rent, bills and food costs.

The government says it "holds the distinguished service of the Gurkhas in the highest regard and remains firmly committed to supporting the welfare of Gurkha veterans and their families".

Many Gurkhas disagree and want their pensions increased.

Indumati lives in a small two-bedroom flat with her friend Devisara Rana in central Reading.

Squeezing into her small bedroom I ask her how she feels about her life.

Her friend and local Labour councillor Pratikshya Gurung translates for her.

"She thinks they've been let down a bit and says she would be grateful if the pension was bigger than it is as that would make her living conditions and financial situation better," Pratikshya says.

For those whose husbands fought for the British in the jungles of places like Malaya and Borneo in the1950s and 60s time is now running out.

The Labour MP for Reading Central Matt Rodda says he is well aware of that fact, and he and other MPs have been pressing both the previous Conservative government and the current Labour one to improve older Gurkha's pension rights.

He says he is also trying to make sure they and their families get all the help they need.

Unable to read or write, many of them rely on younger relations to navigate the modern world, one very different from the land they grew up in.

The Labour MP says: "It's so important we show our support for these elderly people. They served this country with distinction over decades and decades."

The Ministry of Defence says: "The government holds the distinguished service of the Gurkhas in the highest regard and remains firmly committed to supporting the welfare of Gurkha veterans and their families.

"We will continue to work with partners in both Nepal and the UK to ensure Gurkha veterans and their families receive the support and recognition they deserve."

With Pratikshya again translating, I speak to Indumati's close friend Devisara Rana, whose husband and son are no longer with us.

She says she is at peace with the fact all her worldly possessions fit in a bedroom that is no more than 12ft long, by eight feet wide.

Pratikshya tells me all Devisara wants now is to go back to Nepal, but fears she will be unable to afford the trip.

"She doesn't know how long she has got to live but that however many days she does have left she wants to spend those days with her family," she says.

"She just wants to be able to go home one last time."

Do you have a story BBC Berkshire should cover?

articles.title: Family of Alex Pretti speaks out in exclusive interview: 'They murdered our child'
articles.summary: Pretti was shot and killed by federal officers on Jan. 24.
articles.body:
Seven months after 37-year-old Alex Pretti was shot and killed by two federal immigration officers in Minneapolis, his grieving family said they want "accountability" in their first television interview.

"We've seen what happened. The videos are pretty clear. But we want justice. We want accountability for the people that did this to Alex," his father, Michael Pretti, said in the exclusive interview with "Good Morning America" co-anchor George Stephanopoulos while joined by his wife and daughter.

Alex Pretti , an American citizen and ICU nurse for the Department of Veterans Affairs, was killed on Jan. 24, roughly two weeks after fellow U.S. citizen Renee Good was shot and killed by an ICE officer in Minneapolis during the Trump administration's "Operation Metro Surge" immigration crackdown. Both shootings sparked nationwide outrage and demands for accountability over federal officers' deadly use of force in Minneapolis.

Michael Pretti said his son was observing immigration activity when the shooting occurred.

"He cared deeply about his community. Minneapolis was his community. He wanted people to be treated fairly, no matter what walk of life, what their background was," Michael Pretti said.

Watch the interview with the Prettis and George Stephanopoulos on "Good Morning America," airing Tuesday, Aug. 25, at 7 a.m.

Eyewitness video shows that Alex Pretti appeared to be recording when a federal officer shoves a woman into him. He seems to try to help her, and then both of his hands are visible -- one holding a phone and the other held up, seemingly to protect himself from pepper spray -- when he's wrestled to the ground. His firearm, which he had a legal permit to carry, was removed by an officer while he was on the ground and before approximately 10 shots were fired, the video shows.

A minute-by-minute timeline of the fatal shooting of Alex Pretti involving federal agents

His parents said they found out their son had been shot while watching the coverage of the shooting on the news. His mother said she recognized her son's jacket and sunglasses from the footage.

"That's how we found out, watching it on TV. Watching our son be shot ten times on TV," Michael Pretti said.

"In the back," Susan Pretti, Alex's mother, added.

"I was not shocked that he helped somebody. My shock is that he was murdered and no one has given us the complete truth or anyone has been held accountable. And it's been seven months," Susan Pretti said.

"What did he do to deserve to be murdered? To be left cold, on the ground, dead, my child? What did he do?" she asked.

In the wake of the deadly shooting, some Trump administration officials were quick to blame Alex Pretti. Former Border Patrol Commander Greg Bovino said it looked like Pretti wanted "to do maximum damage and massacre law enforcement," and then-Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem claimed he "committed an act of domestic terrorism."

Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller posted on social media that he was an "assassin" and "domestic terrorist."

When asked about the response, Michael Pretti said, "There was more effort in vilifying him than pursuing justice, investigating this."

After video of him in a confrontation with federal agents 11 days before the shooting surfaced on social media, President Donald Trump called Alex Pretti an "agitator" and "perhaps" an "insurrectionist" in a social media post.

Asked what it felt like to hear those things said about their family member, his sister, Micayla Pretti, said, "I don't think you would like my answer."

"It's so un-presidential," Michael Pretti said. "It's ridiculous that, you know, the leader of the free world speaks that way about an American citizen."

Susan Pretti said she wants an apology for what was said about her son. "Why shouldn't we get one?" she asked.

The Department of Justice opened a federal civil rights investigation into the shooting. Steve Schleicher, an attorney for the Pretti family, told ABC News that they don't know where that stands or what information they've gathered.

"They at least have the right to know who shot Alex Pretti," Schleicher said. "They have the right to be consulted with meaningfully, they have the right to meet with the prosecutors, they have the right to have the process not drag on too long. They have the right to be informed, and that's just not being done here."

In a letter to then-Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche last month, Schleicher said that the U.S. attorney in Minnesota met with the Pretti family on July 13 but that "the meeting raised more questions than answers."

2nd Amendment backlash follows portrayal of Alex Pretti by some Trump administration officials

A DOJ spokesperson said in a statement to ABC News, "As is standard protocol, family member communications, if any, come at a later stage of a case, such as at indictment, initial appearance, plea, trial, or sentencing. Communications with family do not typically occur during an investigation."

The Department of Homeland Security and FBI are also involved in the investigation, the DOJ said. A DHS spokesperson told ABC News that the investigation remains active, while the FBI declined to comment.

ABC News asked the White House if Trump and Stephen Miller still stand by what they said about Alex Pretti, but they did not answer the question.

A DHS spokesperson said the agency "works to give the American people accurate information as quickly as possible. These statements were made based on information received on the ground from CBP."

"This is a law enforcement matter and an active investigation and we refer you to FBI for further questions. We urge individuals not to impede any law enforcement action and ICE operations," the spokesperson said.

Asked what justice looks like for them, Micayla Pretti said she wants the names of the agents who shot her brother officially released.

"They murdered our child," Susan Pretti said. "People need to be held responsible when they murder people in this country. Period."

Editor's note: This story has been updated.

articles.title: ‘Perfectly fine with my body’: Danish PM blasts plastic surgeon’s beauty advice
articles.summary: Mette Frederiksen, Denmark’s second female prime minister, is one of Europe’s longest-serving and most experienced leaders.
articles.body: COPENHAGEN, Denmark — Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen is fed up with getting unsolicited beauty advice. The 48-year-old wrote Monday on Instagram that she had just returned home from a trip to Ukraine, where she was exposed to air raid sirens in the ongoing war, only to find a message by a plastic surgeon offering to “fix that little spot on your nose.” “I’ve lost count of how many messages I’ve received over the years about my appearance,” Frederiksen wrote. “Especially that I have ugly teeth and thin hair. That I have an ugly ‘wart’ on my nose and well-meaning advice to get some Botox.” The prime minister of the Nordic country posted a screenshot of the plastic surgeon’s offer on Instagram but without identifying him. She also posted her response: “Oh no. I’m happy with my body — I really don’t need a male plastic surgeon to have an opinion about it!” Frederiksen, a Social Democrat and Denmark’s second female prime minister, is now in her third term, making her one of Europe’s longest-serving and most experienced leaders. She has led the European Union and NATO member country since mid-2019. She has pledged to maintain a firm stance against U.S. President Donald Trump’s ambitions for Greenland, the kingdom’s semiautonomous territory, and continue supporting Ukraine against Russia’s war of aggression. On Instagram, Frederiksen stressed that she does not interfere with other people’s looks and that “I’m perfectly fine with my body — as it is when you’re a woman approaching 50.” She added that “if you’re going to write to me (and you’re more than welcome to), I hope you’ll use your time to talk about something more meaningful. Not my nose.” The prime minister also said that those unsolicited beauty tips and suggestions made her feel “indignant” and that “today, I’m sending an extra loving thought to all of you who have to put up with the ‘perfect imperfections’ we all walk around with every day.”

articles.title: US judge rejects Ghislaine Maxwell's 'frivolous' appeal against conviction
articles.summary: The former Jeffrey Epstein accomplice loses her latest effort to be released from prison.
articles.body:
Ghislaine Maxwell's latest bid to overturn her sex trafficking conviction has been rejected by a US judge, who dismissed her claims as "frivolous" and "meritless".

The 64-year-old is serving a 20-year prison sentence for her role in procuring girls for the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein after being found guilty in December 2021.

Maxwell had appealed against her five felony convictions, claiming her constitutional rights had been "violated in multiple respects".

But a New York judge flatly rejected the appeal, describing it as "lengthy and rambling".

Maxwell said Epstein-related documents released by the US Justice Department earlier this year supported her case that she had been wrongly convicted.

But the judge ruled that "far from exculpating her, it incriminates her or reinforces the correctness" of her conviction.

The judge also said her appeal "falls very far from the mark", adding: "Nearly all its claims are procedurally barred; the overwhelming testimonial and documentary evidence adduced at trial conclusively established her guilt; and her petition's claims are demonstrably meritless, and generally based on speculation, distortions, and/or outright falsehoods.

"There is no fact that Maxwell fairly puts in dispute that has any potential to disturb the outcome of her trial."

The judge warned Maxwell against making further appeals, saying it "would not be taken in good faith" by the court.

Maxwell was found guilty in 2021 of facilitating Epstein's abuse. Prosecutors said she recruited and groomed girls, some as young as 14, between 1994 and 2004, before they were abused by Epstein, who died in prison in 2019.

Maxwell appeared virtually before the US House Oversight Committee in February this year but refused to answer questions, invoking her right to remain silent as she pleaded the Fifth Amendment.

Republican House Oversight Committee chairman James Comer said the situation was "very disappointing", adding: "We had many questions to ask about the crimes she and Epstein committed, as well as questions about potential co-conspirators."

Maxwell has previously sought a pardon from US President Donald Trump.

When asked last October whether he would consider pardoning Maxwell, Trump said he "wouldn't consider it or not consider it", adding: "I don't know anything about it, so I will speak to the [Department of Justice]."

The US Senate last month passed a resolution declaring its opposition to a presidential pardon for Maxwell.

articles.title: Israeli attacks kill five in Gaza, including two children, medics say
articles.summary: An Israeli strike on Monday killed a four-year-old boy, while a 10-year-old girl was hit by a bullet inside her tent, according to medics and relatives.
articles.body:
Israeli air strikes and gunfire in the Gaza Strip on Monday killed at least five Palestinians, including two children, according to health officials.

Medics and relatives said a 10-year-old girl was shot dead while inside her family's tent in the southern city of Khan Younis.

A four-year-old boy was meanwhile killed in an air strike in Bureij refugee camp in central Gaza.

The Israeli military said it was not aware of the incident in Khan Younis, but that it had issued an evacuation order in Bureij before carrying out a strike on what it described as a Hamas weapons storage facility.

At least 1,296 Palestinians, including 300 children, have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since a ceasefire between Israel and Hamas took effect last October, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry.

The Israeli military says four of its soldiers have been killed in Palestinian attacks in Gaza over the same period.

Amal Abu Khater, 10, was hit by a bullet in her back while eating in her tent in the central al-Sattar al-Gharbi area of Khan Younis on Monday, according to her family. They rushed the girl to hospital but medics told them on arrival that she had died of her wounds.

"She was eating sweets," her grandmother, Samira Abu Labda, told Reuters news agency. "Why did she have to die like this? What wrong did this child do?"

In Bureij, Gaza's Hamas-run Civil Defence agency said its first responders recovered the body of four-year-old Hassan al-Qatrawi from beneath the rubble of his family's home following an air strike on a neighbouring building. His mother and sister were pulled out alive.

Pictures of the aftermath showed people clambering over a large crater and searching nearby piles of concrete and metal.

The Israeli military said it had ordered residents to evacuate the area before the strike, and that the target was one of five Hamas weapons storage facilities and a launch site that were bombed in central and northern Gaza on Monday.

It alleged that the facilities had been "established inside mosques and alongside humanitarian infrastructure" in violation of international law.

One of the mosques that was struck was in the town of Deir al-Balah, just south of Bureij.

Aerial video footage released by the military appeared to show a large explosion destroying two structures adjoining the main prayer hall.

At the scene on Tuesday, resident Mohammed Abu Amra rejected the claim that the mosque had been used to store weapons.

"They are bombing the book of our Lord," he said while holding up a damaged Quran.

The UN's humanitarian office also said that three UN warehouses in Deir al-Balah were damaged in an air strike on Monday, one of them significantly.

In the Sheikh Radwan neighbourhood of Gaza City, to the north, residents said a water desalination plant was bombed at a time when they were suffering from water shortages.

The Israeli military said it targeted a Hamas weapons storage facilities near the plant.

Hamas spokesman Hazem Qassem condemned the attack, calling it a "further attempt to deprive [Gaza's population] of all means of survival".

At least three other people were killed in Israeli strikes across Gaza on Monday.

Among them were two brothers, Mohammed and Ibrahim Abu Asad, whose tent in Deir al-Balah was bombed overnight, according to Palestinian media.

The Israeli military said Mohammed was an operative in Hamas's elite Nukhba force who had taken part in the 7 October 2023 attack on southern Israel, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 were taken hostage.

Israel responded to the attack by launching a military campaign in Gaza, during which more than 73,430 people have been killed, according to the territory's health ministry.

In Bureij, Gaza's Hamas-run Civil Defence agency said its first responders recovered the body of four-year-old Hassan al-Qatrawi from beneath the rubble of his family's home following an air strike on a neighbouring building. His mother and sister were pulled out alive.
Pictures of the aftermath showed people clambering over a large crater and searching nearby piles of concrete and metal.

The Israeli military said it had ordered residents to evacuate the area before the strike, and that the target was one of five Hamas weapons storage facilities and a launch site that were bombed in central and northern Gaza on Monday.
It alleged that the facilities had been "established inside mosques and alongside humanitarian infrastructure" in violation of international law.
One of the mosques that was struck was in the town of Deir al-Balah, just south of Bureij.
Aerial video footage released by the military appeared to show a large explosion destroying two structures adjoining the main prayer hall.
At the scene on Tuesday, resident Mohammed Abu Amra rejected the claim that the mosque had been used to store weapons.
"They are bombing the book of our Lord," he said while holding up a damaged Quran.
The UN's humanitarian office also said that three UN warehouses in Deir al-Balah were damaged in an air strike on Monday, one of them significantly.
In the Sheikh Radwan neighbourhood of Gaza City, to the north, residents said a water desalination plant was bombed at a time when they were suffering from water shortages.
The Israeli military said it targeted a Hamas weapons storage facilities near the plant.
Hamas spokesman Hazem Qassem condemned the attack, calling it a "further attempt to deprive [Gaza's population] of all means of survival".
At least three other people were killed in Israeli strikes across Gaza on Monday.
Among them were two brothers, Mohammed and Ibrahim Abu Asad, whose tent in Deir al-Balah was bombed overnight, according to Palestinian media.

The Israeli military said Mohammed was an operative in Hamas's elite Nukhba force who had taken part in the 7 October 2023 attack on southern Israel, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 were taken hostage.
Israel responded to the attack by launching a military campaign in Gaza, during which more than 73,430 people have been killed, according to the territory's health ministry.

articles.title: Denmark's left-wing PM warns: 'Big enemy has started to grow from within' as Europe faces migrant reckoning
articles.summary: Mette Frederiksen's stance on Denmark immigration and border control puts her at odds with Spain's PM, as she names failed integration and Islamist extremism as key threats.
articles.body: Denmark's left-wing prime minister, Mette Frederiksen, has sent shockwaves throughout the European left after recent comments about the Scandinavian nation's — and the continent's — failure to deal with radical Islam among migrant communities. Her comments come after the mass migration chaos in the Spanish exclave of Ceuta, when Frederiksen criticized the actions of Spain's leftist leader, Pedro Sánchez, during a special session on Ceuta in the Danish Parliament.  Responding to a question from a far-left legislator on Denmark’s apparent lack of "solidarity" with Spain against "anti-democratic forces" pressuring Europe, Frederiksen said, "If we talk about undemocratic forces, then Russia is our biggest enemy. The problem is that a big enemy has started to grow from within, and it is foreigners who have come to Europe," according to an English translation. MIGRANT CRISIS PUSHES ITALY TO RESTORE BORDER CHECKS WITH SPAIN, TESTING EUROPE'S OPEN-BORDER SYSTEM While not singling out Denmark's integrated immigrant population, she continued, "It is Hamas supporters. It is people who commit terror against European societies. It is people who do not recognize our fundamental European values. It is people who sympathize with some of the darkest forces in this world. So, Europe is threatened. The problem is that we are threatened both from outside and now from within, but it is not because of a disagreement between the Danish and Spanish governments, but because of people with an Islamic background who do not want the open, free European society, unfortunately." Sweden-based foreign policy expert and author Daniel Schatz told Fox News Digital, "What is striking is not that a conservative politician is talking about illegal immigration, failed integration and Islamist extremism, it is that one of Europe’s leading center-left prime ministers is saying it in such blunt terms. That tells you how far the European immigration debate has shifted." PORTUGAL ENACTS 'BURQA LAW' LARGELY PROHIBITING FACE COVERINGS IN PUBLIC Frederiksen came to power in Denmark’s 2019 elections on what Reuters called a "platform of radical reforms to reach climate targets, lowering the pension age for manual workers - and stricter migration policies." Denmark already had some of the strongest asylum laws in Europe before 2019, including a 2018 law targeting "parallel societies." That law allowed the government to "demolish or sell off social housing areas where more than half of residents are from a ‘non-Western’ background," if certain criteria were met, and refugees in those areas are not eligible for family reunion. In 2021, Frederiksen introduced a new deportation law allowing for refugees to be returned to their country of origin, if Denmark deemed it safe, even if Denmark had no diplomatic relations with that country, and even as the European Commission deemed Danish legislation on transferring asylum seekers to third countries while their claims were processed "incompatible with EU law." Since June, Frederiksen has been a leading voice in opposition to the immigration policies of Spain’s Pedro Sánchez, telling Parliament, "It is no secret that I and the Spanish Prime Minister deeply disagree on immigration policy… I and we will not accept that Danish society has to pay the price for decisions in Spain that we fundamentally disagree with." On Aug 1, Frederiksen joined conservative Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and 20 other EU government leaders in a letter saying the EU "cannot allow mass crossings, the instrumentalization of migration or other hybrid threats to create the perception that illegal entry into the European Union is possible." ITALY-SPAIN BORDER FEUD EXPOSES EUROPE’S DEEPENING IMMIGRATION DIVIDE The two, currently the only female heads of government in the EU, followed that letter with an Aug 10 joint statement saying they "are both proud of Europe’s Christian cultural heritage and we want to protect it. We expect that those who arrive in our countries and choose to make Europe their home respect our values and do not try to impose ways of life that we do not share. We believe that this is the right path to protect Europe and our common values. And we believe that millions of Europeans share this conviction." Emma Schubart of the Henry Jackson Society told Fox News Digital, "Frederiksen is right to name the ‘enemy within’. Europe has spent years pretending that uncontrolled migration and failed integration come without consequences. They do not… Parallel societies have taken root, Islamist extremism has been allowed to fester and support for groups such as Hamas is no longer confined to the margins. Denmark understands the cost." Daniel Schatz said Frederiksen "is essentially arguing that Europe faces threats from two directions: Russia from outside and anti-democratic extremism from within. For a center-left European leader, that is remarkably strong language." He noted Frederiksen’s "political formula has been straightforward: protect Denmark’s generous system of public benefits and social services, control the border and deny the populist right a monopoly on immigration. For an American audience, that is probably the most important thing to understand about the Danish model." Frederiksen’s position is important, he said, because she did not move politically "because Danish voters suddenly became concerned about immigration. She moved because she realized years ago that many of them already were." He added, "The important distinction is that this is not an argument that immigrants are inherently criminal. It is an argument that a democratic society must be willing to confront failed integration when it occurs." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Schubart added, "Other leaders now need to show the same courage, secure their borders, deport those with no right to remain and make clear that integration into our laws and values is not optional." Reuters contributed to this report.

articles.title: How Often Should You Replace Running Shoes? Podiatrists Explain
articles.summary: Running in worn-out shoes can lead to aches, pains and injuries. Podiatrists break down how many miles your running shoes should last and when it’s time for a new pair.
articles.body: We don’t always have the answers, but we have some people on speed dial who do — which is why we present to you our series FYI where we have experts explain if hair removal cream is actually bad, how often you should change your towels and more. Running shoes don’t last forever, even if they still look fine from the outside. Over time, the cushioning and support inside break down and running in shoes that have lost their structure can leave your feet, knees and joints unsupported, making you more prone to aches, pains and even injuries. The tricky part is that this breakdown happens gradually, so it’s easy to keep running in shoes that have quietly stopped doing their job. To find out exactly when it’s time to retire your running shoes — and what to watch for before your body starts sending its own warning signals — I talked to doctors who explained how mileage and body type factor into the equation. I’ve also rounded up some podiatrist- and editor-approved running shoes worth adding to your cart if you find that it’s time for a fresh pair. How often do running shoes need to be replaced? Most doctors say mileage is the clearest benchmark for retiring your running shoes. “In general, a running shoe should last somewhere between 300 and 500 miles,” says Dr. Dietmar Walter, head of podiatry at Stride Soles, a custom orthotics company. “However, the exact length depends on your weight, running surface and of course the shoe type.” Treadmills tend to be gentler on shoes, while consistently running on pavement or concrete can wear down cushioning a bit faster, since there’s less natural give to absorb the impact. Body weight in particular can make a dramatic difference in how quickly a shoe wears out. “I see many patients over 200 pounds only last 200 miles in their shoes, while someone under 140 pounds might last over 550 miles,” says Walter. That’s a gap of more than 350 miles between the two groups, underscoring why there’s no single mileage number that works for every runner — and why paying attention to how your shoes feel matters just as much as counting miles. What are signs you need to replace your running shoes? Mileage is a helpful guideline, but your body often sends signals before you hit a specific number. “A good sign that your shoes need replacing is if you are starting to get unexpected aches and pains — like achilles tendonitis, shin splints or plantar fascia pain,” says Dr. Milica McDowell, a doctor of physical therapy and co-author of Walk: Rediscover the Most Natural Way to Boost Your Health and Longevity ― One Step at a Time. If new discomfort starts creeping in during or after your runs, it’s worth taking a closer look at your shoes before the problem gets worse. Walter also says you can examine your shoe to look for signs of excessive wear. These are the things he says point to your shoes needing to be replaced: Look at the midsole: If it looks compressed, has striations (grooves or ridges) in it or has uneven wear, it’s likely time to replace the shoes.Check the inside back of your shoes: Look at where your achilles rests against the back of your shoes. If that area is torn or there is missing material, this is a major sign to replace your shoe as your foot is no longer being held securely as you run.Examine the bottom of your shoes: Simply checking the rubber at the bottom of your shoes is an easy way to see if there is excessive wear. If you notice foam through the bottom or areas where there is no tread, it’s likely time to replace your shoes. The best running sneakers for when yours need replacing If it is time to replace your running shoes, Walter recommends a few of his favorites below. I also included running sneakers that NBC Selected editors swear by. They each have at least a four-star average rating from 100 customers or more. Walter recommends this shoe for its plush, responsive foam cushioning and structural support rods that guide a smooth transition from heel to toe. The breathable mesh upper offers a comfortable, snug fit, while the durable rubber outsole delivers reliable traction — making it a solid, everyday pick for runners logging daily miles. Walter does note that it’s not the softest landing, but says that firmness is what keeps it working well after hundreds of miles. This shoe is also available for men. These shoes, which are available for men or women, come recommended by Walter because they have a 3.5 millimeter of outsole rubber, while the average shoe has 3.1. “If you are someone running outside in variable concrete city blocks, this will make a difference over the long run,” he says. These running shoes also offer a soft, cushioned ride with a supportive, breathable knit upper designed to lock the foot in place. They also have a durable rubber outsole that delivers reliable traction on the road. The shoes have been given theAmerican Podiatric Medical Association (APMA) Seal of Acceptance, which is awarded to shoes that promote good foot health. This style is also available for men and women and has a highly-cushioned sole to support you as you run. “The cushioning keeps my feet incredibly comfortable, and while it’s on the softer side, I never feel like I’m sinking into it,” says NBC Selected reporter Zoe Malin, who has worn these for both shorter jogs and longer runs. “The shoes have a bouncy feel and a gentle rocker-shaped outsole for smooth heel-toe transitions.” These sneakers have a breathable mesh upper and a grippy sole for traction. I’ve run three half marathons in these sneakers and have been wildly impressed by how they hold up. As a plus size runner, support is key and these have held up as I’ve logged lots of miles. I also have flat feet and find that these have the perfect amount of arch support for me. The sneakers, which are also available for men, have a padded tongue and collar for comfort and are on the wider side. The Clifton 10 has ultralight, plush cushioning in the sole and a breathable jacquard knit upper. They also have a wide toe box and a double-lace lock system to keep your foot secure as you move. “In addition to a gentle rocker outsole that keeps me moving forward at whatever pace I set, they have great traction and controlled bounce,” says Malin. “The foam also sufficiently cushions my feet so they never feel tired, but it’s not so soft that I’m sinking into it.” While this pair is for women, Hoka has the same style on sale for men. articles.title: 9/11 victim's identity emerges nearly 25 years later after DNA breakthrough cracks mystery
articles.summary: A first-of-its-kind forensic genealogy technique helped New York City investigators identify a World Trade Center victim nearly 25 years after 9/11.
articles.body: Nearly 25 years after the Sept. 11 attacks, a family has finally received an answer after New York City investigators used a first-of-its-kind DNA and genealogy technique to identify a woman killed at the World Trade Center. The adult woman, whose name is being withheld at her family’s request, is the first World Trade Center victim identified through forensic investigative genetic genealogy, New York City officials announced Sunday. Her identification marks the 1,654th person identified from remains recovered after the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, which killed 2,753 people in New York City. 9/11 MUSEUM CEO REFLECTS ON LASTING IMPACT OF TERROR ATTACKS AS AMERICA MARKS 250TH BIRTHDAY The breakthrough came through a collaboration between the Office of Chief Medical Examiner, and the NYPD’s Investigative Genetic Genealogy Squad. The technique pairs specialized DNA analysis with genealogy research to generate leads that are then confirmed through forensic testing. "As we approach the 25th anniversary of the horrific September 11 attacks, we honor the nearly 3,000 people whose lives were stolen that day," NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a statement. "We remain committed to the families who have spent 25 years waiting for answers." REMAINS FOUND IN UTAH DESERT 28 YEARS AGO WITH HELP OF A PSYCHIC FINALLY IDENTIFIED THROUGH DNA GENEALOGY Forensic investigative genetic genealogy has emerged as a powerful tool in cold cases, allowing investigators to trace family connections from DNA evidence and identify people who may otherwise have remained unknown. Chief Medical Examiner Dr. Graham said the new method could help advance the city’s long-running effort to identify those killed in the attacks. WOMAN FOUND IN SHALLOW GRAVE ID’D AFTER 44 YEARS AS MILLIONAIRE TIED TO ESTATE MURDER PLOT "This sacred commitment is propelled by our dedication to apply the most innovative scientific techniques," Graham said. "FIGG represents a promising new addition to our toolkit." Officials said they are also using renewed family outreach and continued DNA retesting to link recovered remains to victims already identified. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP But the work remains unfinished. About 1,099 World Trade Center victims, roughly 40% of those killed, have yet to be identified. The woman is the first newly identified World Trade Center victim since August 2025, officials said.

articles.title: Did India hit Kirana Hills during Op Sindoor? Ex-CDS Anil Chauhan clears air
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Former Chief of Defence Staff Anil Chauhan on Tuesday said India may have hit Pakistan's Kirana Hills during Operation Sindoor last year, b.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former Chief of Defence Staff Anil Chauhan on Tuesday said India may have hit Pakistan's Kirana Hills during Operation Sindoor last year, but the strike was unintentional.Speaking at the âVIMARSHâ event on Operation Sindoor and its aftermath at the Vivekanand International Foundation, Chauhan said Indian loitering missions sent to search for radars around Sargodha ran out of fuel and ended up hitting Kirana Hills -- a site associated with Pakistan's nuclear facilities."At occasions, it's been asked whether Kirana Hills were hit or not, which is where their (Pakistan's) nuclear facilities are... Before those strikes, we had sent in a lot of loitering missions at Sargodha and Kirana Hills is about 10 kilometers north of Sargodha," Chauhan said."So the loitering mission is looking for radars which are in and around Sargodha, and it has a lifetime, which means it will loiter for about 2 hours and once it does not find a target, it comes down and hits somewhere. It must have come and hit one of those hills. So that could be one of the reasons as to what people asked, because Pakistani media also showed some kind of images in which there was smoke coming out from Kirana Hills," he added.Chauhan also revealed details of another episode during the operation, saying the Air Chief sought his approval to strike Sargodha after Pakistan requested talks. However the target was changed to Bholari due to bad weather."Once the Pakistanis had picked up the phone and said they wanted to talk at about 10 AM. The Air Chief asked me whether he should strike Sargodha, I said, Go ahead. I said, could you please identify two more targets, so one of the targets he identified was Skardu," Chauhan said."We gave a yes, but after some time, the weather was bad over it and they had to change over to Bholari," he added.During his address, Chauhan also stressed that military decisions involve varying levels of risk and must be assessed against the political objectives they are intended to achieve."Each option has a certain kind of risk involved in it, and also it will satisfy the political need for which it was to be used. So, itâs an interplay between risk and attainment of political objectives," he said.Chauhan said the operation remains relevant nearly 15 months after its major active phase ended. He said its assessment should take into account deficiencies identified during the operation, measures taken to address them and the changing nature of warfare.He added that these factors, along with wider global uncertainties, are creating new challenges for military planners.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: China warns US of retaliation if Trump's 'Economic D-Day' sanctions hit their Iran oil trade
articles.summary: China News: China has warned that it could take retaliatory measures if the United States significantly expands secondary sanctions targeting Chinese companies do.
articles.body: China has warned that it could take retaliatory measures if the United States significantly expands secondary sanctions targeting Chinese companies doing business with Iran, according to reporting by the Financial Times.The warning came after the Trump administration on Monday announced new sanctions targeting companies in Hong Kong and mainland China as part of a broader crackdown on Iran's oil trade. The measures, however, did not target major Chinese financial institutions, FT reported.A Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said on Tuesday that Beijing would take "all necessary measures" to safeguard its rights and interests, while reiterating China's opposition to what it described as unilateral sanctions lacking a basis in international law or United Nations Security Council authorisation.The spokesperson also called for de-escalation and a return to dialogue and negotiations.China is Iran's largest oil customer, with Chinese buyers accounting for about 90% of Iran's oil exports. While China's state-owned refiners largely comply with US sanctions on Iranian crude, smaller private refiners, known as "teapots", continue to import and process Iranian oil.The United States has sanctioned some of those refiners this year, but Beijing has instructed Chinese companies not to comply with such measures.The prospect of broader US secondary sanctions comes at a sensitive point in US-China relations. US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are expected to meet in Washington next month, with the leaders expected to discuss extending a one-year truce in their trade dispute.Wang Dong, a senior scholar at Peking University, told FT that Beijing would defend its national interests if Washington moved ahead with broader sanctions, though he said it remained unclear whether the US threat was serious or a negotiating tactic.Zhu Feng, an international relations expert at Nanjing University, told the newspaper that China was also keen to see the conflict between the United States and Iran de-escalate.Zhu said continued restrictions on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz were putting additional pressure on the global economy and could pose a greater risk to China because of its dependence on Middle Eastern oil supplies."From a Chinese perspective, we don't want to get involved in a US-Iranian fight," Zhu told FT.Chinese officials have also stepped up diplomatic contacts in the Middle East. President Xi Jinping recently met Jordan's King Abdullah II, while Foreign Minister Wang Yi held talks with his Kuwaiti counterpart, with Iran and the Gaza war among the issues discussed, according to the Financial Times.Zhu said China's message to Tehran was that Beijing wanted peace talks to continue.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
